problem: Current deep learning approaches for protein-ligand binding affinity prediction are limited by the scarcity of high-quality experimental structures with annotated binding affinities.
approach: The authors introduce SAIR, a large-scale dataset of 5.2 million protein-ligand 3D structures with associated activity data curated from ChEMBL and BindingDB, with computationally folded structures using Boltz-1x model.
contribution: SAIR provides the largest publicly available dataset of protein-ligand structures with activity annotations and establishes benchmarks showing machine learning models outperform traditional scoring functions, though neither exhibit high correlation with ground truth affinities yet.

problem: State-of-the-art autoregressive LLMs exhibit unreliability when generating structured outputs, which is critical for controllable generation and agentic communication.
approach: The paper proposes Self-adaptive Schema Scaffolding (S3), which leverages diffusion LLMs' global information-sharing mechanism and reverse reasoning capability to generate structured outputs by initiating a schematic template as a starting state.
contribution: S3 substantially improves controllable generation in diffusion LLMs across structure adherence, content fidelity, and faithfulness compared to prompt optimization approaches.

problem: Standard RLHF pipelines redundantly train reward models then derive value functions, when pretraining a value model directly would be more efficient and stable.
approach: Decoupled Value Policy Optimization (DVPO) pretrains a Global Value Model offline and freezes it as a universal critic, enabling policy-only optimization without online critic learning or trajectory sampling.
contribution: DVPO matches or surpasses state-of-the-art RLHF methods on MT-Bench, Alpaca-Eval, and Arena-Hard while reframing RLHF as policy optimization guided by a single pretrained value model.

problem: Audio and music generation under flexible multimodal control signals requires both a unified framework for integrating diverse modal conditions and large-scale high-quality training data.
approach: AudioX proposes a unified framework with a Multimodal Adaptive Fusion module to integrate text, video, image, and audio conditions, trained on a large-scale dataset IF-caps comprising over 7 million curated samples.
contribution: AudioX achieves superior performance across multiple tasks, especially in text-to-audio and text-to-music generation, demonstrating powerful instruction-following potential with multimodal control.

problem: Multi-turn LLM agents suffer from reward sparsity in outcome-based training, leading to advantage collapse and poor credit assignment across long trajectories.
approach: Information Gain-based Policy Optimization (IGPO) provides dense, turn-level rewards by modeling each interaction as incremental information acquisition about the ground truth, combining intrinsic and outcome-level supervision.
contribution: IGPO consistently outperforms strong baselines on in-domain and out-of-domain benchmarks with higher accuracy and improved sample efficiency.

problem: Large multimodal models are executed monolithically, underutilizing heterogeneous accelerators (NPUs, GPUs, DSPs) in modern SoCs and leading to high latency on battery-powered devices.
approach: NANOMIND is a hardware-software co-design framework that breaks multimodal models into modular components mapped to their ideal accelerators with module-level dynamic offloading, token-aware buffer management, and low-bit computation kernels.
contribution: NANOMIND enables a battery-powered device to run LlaVA-OneVision-qwen2-05B for nearly 20.8 hours while cutting energy consumption by 42.3% and GPU memory by 11.2%.

problem: Large language models remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks despite advances in safety alignment, and existing attack methods lack interpretability and robustness.
approach: Head-Masked Nullspace Steering (HMNS) performs circuit-level intervention by identifying causally responsible attention heads, suppressing their write paths via column masking, and injecting perturbations constrained to the orthogonal complement of the muted subspace.
contribution: HMNS attains state-of-the-art jailbreak success rates with fewer queries than prior methods across multiple benchmarks and strong safety defenses.

problem: Structure-based de novo protein binder design typically relies on either conditional generation or sequence optimization, failing to leverage both paradigms' strengths.
approach: Complexa unifies generative and hallucination paradigms through flow-based latent generation and test-time optimization using Teddymer, a large-scale dataset of synthetic binder-target pairs combined with high-quality experimental multimers.
contribution: Complexa sets state-of-the-art in computational binder design benchmarks with markedly higher in-silico success rates and novel test-time optimization strategies surpassing previous hallucination methods.

problem: Model-based deep reinforcement learning from pixels fails to capture small, task-critical objects in complex, dynamic scenes due to pixel-level reconstruction losses.
approach: OC-STORM integrates object-centric representations from pretrained segmentation into a learned world model, conditioning on minimal annotated frames to track decision-relevant object dynamics and inter-object interactions.
contribution: OC-STORM significantly outperforms STORM on Atari 100k and achieves state-of-the-art sample efficiency on challenging Hollow Knight boss fights.

problem: Classical federated learning requires multi-round iterative model exchange with high communication costs and privacy risks; existing one-shot approaches lack practical deployment or require strong assumptions.
approach: Gaussian-Head OFL (GH-OFL) assumes class-conditional Gaussianity of pretrained embeddings, with clients transmitting only sufficient statistics and the server constructing heads via closed-form Gaussian methods, FisherMix, and Proto-Hyper.
contribution: GH-OFL delivers state-of-the-art robustness and accuracy under strong non-IID skew while remaining data-free.

problem: Existing protein-ligand docking benchmarks focus on self-docking which is less practical than cross-docking, and many methods require extensive training frameworks.
approach: PoseX is an open-source benchmark evaluating both self-docking and cross-docking with 718 self-docking and 1,312 cross-docking entries, testing 23 methods including physics-based and AI approaches with post-processing relaxation.
contribution: PoseX reveals that AI-based approaches consistently outperform physics-based methods overall, and combining AI modeling with physics-based post-processing achieves excellent performance.

problem: Universal image restoration under unknown degradation types is challenged by discriminative restorers and UNet-based diffusion priors that oversmooth, hallucinate, or drift.
approach: LucidFlux adapts a large diffusion transformer (Flux.1) with a lightweight dual-branch conditioner injecting signals from the degraded input and lightly restored proxy, using timestep- and layer-adaptive modulation and caption-free semantic alignment.
contribution: LucidFlux consistently surpasses strong baselines across seven metrics with clear visual gains in realism, detail, and artifact suppression, achieving caption-free restoration without text prompts.

problem: Multi-model inference systems experience explosive Key-Value cache memory consumption as each model maintains separate caches for identical prompts, forcing eviction and recomputation.
approach: Identical Cache Reuse (ICaRus) allows multiple models to share identical KV caches by decomposing decoder-only Transformers into a logical encoder and decoder, fine-tuning only the decoder while freezing the encoder.
contribution: ICaRus eliminates cache memory explosion and redundant recomputation while enabling cross-model reuse of KV caches for new tokens, achieving both efficiency and scalability.

problem: Pan-cancer screening in large-scale CT scans struggles with localizing diverse tiny lesions due to extreme foreground-background imbalance.
approach: GF-Screen employs a Glance model to localize diseased regions and a Focus model to segment lesions, using reinforcement learning with a group relative learning paradigm to select high-advantage predictions and discard low-advantage ones.
contribution: GF-Screen effectively extends RL techniques to pan-cancer screening for the first time, improving efficiency and reducing false positives through glance-and-focus strategy.

problem: Multimodal LLMs struggle to understand and reason over 3D point clouds with high interclass confusion, particularly for standalone point cloud reasoning.
approach: Point-Graph LLM (PGLLM) constructs a graph of point cloud samples with edges encoding visual similarity, retrieves relevant neighbors for in-context prompting, and refines LLM scores via label propagation at test-time.
contribution: PGLLM consistently improves accuracy and robustness over baselines with minimal additional computation cost on 3D datasets and out-of-distribution detection tasks.

problem: Inverse protein folding that designs sequences to fold into target structures lacks explicit mechanisms to reuse fine-grained structure-sequence patterns conserved across natural proteins.
approach: PRISM uses a multimodal retrieval-augmented generation framework that retrieves fine-grained motif representations from known proteins and integrates them with a hybrid self-cross attention decoder.
contribution: PRISM achieves state-of-the-art perplexity and amino acid recovery on multiple benchmarks while improving foldability metrics (RMSD, TM-score, pLDDT).

problem: Radio frequency-based material identification lacks large-scale public datasets and benchmarking of learning-based approaches for fine-grained classification.
approach: RF-MatID provides the first large-scale, wide-band, and geometry-diverse RF dataset with 142k samples across 16 fine-grained categories in frequency- and time-domain, incorporating controlled perturbations in incidence angle and stand-off distance.
contribution: RF-MatID establishes multi-setting benchmarks evaluating deep learning models and assessing robustness under cross-angle and cross-distance shifts for real-world RF-based material identification.

problem: Existing reinforcement finetuning methods for LLMs are inherently on-policy and fail to reuse historical data efficiently, preventing scalability.
approach: ReMix enables off-policy RL by combining mix-policy proximal policy gradient with increased Update-To-Data ratio, KL-Convex policy constraint, and policy reincarnation that transitions from efficiency to convergence.
contribution: ReMix achieves average Pass@1 accuracy of 52.10% on 1.5B and 64.39% on 7B models across five math reasoning benchmarks with significantly fewer rollouts than previous methods.

problem: Current multi-agent systems follow a rigid generate-once-and-deploy paradigm, rendering them brittle for dynamic real-world environments.
approach: MAS² employs a recursive self-generation paradigm with a generator-implementer-rectifier tri-agent team that dynamically composes and adaptively rectifies multi-agent systems using Collaborative Tree Optimization.
contribution: MAS² achieves performance gains up to 19.6% over state-of-the-art MAS on complex scenarios and superior cross-backbone generalization with up to 15.1% improvement on unseen LLMs.

problem: Fine-tuning-as-a-service introduces a threat to LLM safety when models are fine-tuned on poisoned datasets, creating harmful fine-tuning attacks.
approach: Antibody ensures robust safety alignment by optimizing models into a flat loss region for harmful samples, then applies a safety-preservation algorithm during fine-tuning that weights samples to inhibit learning from harmful samples.
contribution: Antibody successfully mitigates harmful fine-tuning attacks while maintaining fine-tuning performance on benign user-submitted datasets.

problem: Long protein sequences are difficult to make, express in cells, or deliver to tissues, and shortening them typically requires costly, time-consuming experimental campaigns.
approach: SCISOR is a discrete diffusion model that deletes letters from sequences by training a denoiser to reverse a noising process that adds insertions to natural sequences.
contribution: SCISOR achieves state-of-the-art predictions of functional deletion effects on ProteinGym and generates shrunken proteins with significantly more realistic structures and better preservation of functional motifs.

problem: Understanding what enables language models to predict text better remains unclear, limiting interpretability and model selection capabilities.
approach: The paper demonstrates that representation dispersion (average pairwise cosine distance among hidden vectors) strongly correlates with perplexity and can be leveraged for model selection, layer identification, and training optimization.
contribution: Measuring dispersion on unlabeled text predicts downstream accuracy in new domains, identifying high-dispersion layers improves retrieval methods, and a simple push-away objective directly improves perplexity.

problem: Long-context reasoning requires accurately identifying relevant information in extensive, noisy input contexts, which standard fine-tuning struggles to do efficiently.
approach: PERK (Parameter Efficient Reasoning over Knowledge) uses nested optimization loops to encode long contexts into low-rank LoRA adapters at test-time, enabling the adapter to serve as a parameter-efficient memory module.
contribution: PERK achieves average performance gains up to 20% on long-context reasoning tasks while maintaining advantages across model scales and matching specialized long-context LLMs.

problem: Narrow domain fine-tuning creates models with unusual properties, but the specific ways fine-tuning modifies neural networks remain poorly understood.
approach: The Activation Difference Lens (ADL) analyzes activation differences between base and finetuned models to detect easily readable biases reflecting overrepresentation of finetuning data.
contribution: ADL recovers the format and general content of finetuning data from activation differences and significantly enhances interpretability agents' ability to identify finetuning objectives.

problem: Understanding how scaling laws relate to task symmetry and architectural choices for geometric tasks remains unclear.
approach: The paper presents an empirical study of scaling behavior in interatomic potential learning, demonstrating that equivariant architectures and higher-order representations exhibit better scaling exponents.
contribution: The analysis reveals that equivariance matters more at larger scales with architecture-dependent exponents, and data and model sizes should scale in tandem for compute-optimal training.

problem: LLMs struggle to intelligently and adaptively gather information in multi-turn conversational settings when interfacing with external environments.
approach: BED-LLM uses sequential Bayesian experimental design to enable LLMs to iteratively choose questions maximizing expected information gain about the task based on previous responses.
contribution: BED-LLM achieves substantial gains across 20 Questions game and user preference inference tasks compared to direct prompting and other adaptive design strategies.

problem: Knowledge editing methods that modify MLP layers often cause significant perturbations to edited models and struggle to preserve knowledge.
approach: Subspace Knowledge Edit (SUIT) identifies and modifies only the subspace of critical features relevant to the edit, constraining perturbations to essential dimensions.
contribution: SUIT dramatically improves knowledge preservation over strong baselines while maintaining high edit efficacy on LLaMA-3-8B, GPT-J-6B, and Qwen2.5-7B models.

problem: Multilingual LLMs often struggle with non-English tasks due to two key failure modes: the multilingual transfer bottleneck and the language consistency bottleneck.
approach: LinguaMap extends logit lens analysis to track language probabilities and semantic similarity layer-by-layer, then applies selective fine-tuning of only final language-control layers using LoRA.
contribution: Selective fine-tuning achieves over 98% language consistency across six languages while fine-tuning only 3-5% of parameters, matching full-scope fine-tuning with fewer resources.

problem: LLM router training requires balancing between accurate but expensive gold-standard data and cheaper but biased preference-based evaluation data.
approach: A causal inference framework casts router training as correcting preference-data bias by viewing evaluation as treatment assignment and addressing conditional average treatment effects.
contribution: The integrative causal router framework delivers more accurate routing and improves the trade-off between inference cost and response quality.

problem: Weight binarization approaches for LLMs either cause severe performance loss through post-training methods or add complexity through training-aware methods that require full-precision latent weights.
approach: A novel framework represents LLMs with multi-kernel Boolean parameters and enables direct fine-tuning in the Boolean domain without latent weights, enhancing representational capacity while reducing complexity.
contribution: The method outperforms recent ultra low-bit quantization and binarization techniques across diverse LLMs.

problem: Existing evaluations of LLM search agents focus solely on final answer accuracy, overlooking how agents reason with and act on external evidence.
approach: SeekBench introduces a process-level evaluation framework operationalizing epistemic competence through metrics derived from an expert-annotated schema of agent traces.
contribution: SeekBench reveals critical behavioral gaps in state-of-the-art agents that answer-only metrics miss, providing granular analysis of groundedness, recovery, and calibration abilities.

problem: Real-time robot manipulation requires asynchronous inference for responsiveness, but naive integration results in execution failures due to inter-chunk discontinuity and intra-chunk inconsistency.
approach: REMAC learns corrective adjustments through masked action chunking to handle mismatches between intended actions and actual execution, with prefix-preserved sampling for inter-chunk continuity.
contribution: REMAC enables faster task execution, maintains robustness across varying delays, and consistently achieves higher completion rates than prior test-time smoothing methods.

problem: Latent reasoning in LLMs can be brittle on challenging, out-of-distribution tasks where robust reasoning is most critical.
approach: Latent Thought Policy Optimization (LTPO) optimizes intermediate latent thought vectors at test-time using online policy gradient guided by confidence-based rewards from the frozen LLM's output distributions.
contribution: LTPO matches or surpasses baselines on standard tasks and delivers substantial improvements on highly challenging AIME benchmarks where existing latent reasoning baselines collapse.

problem: Current molecule LLMs are limited by representing molecules at the atomic level, failing to prioritize synthesizability and predict drug-like properties effectively.
approach: mCLM tokenizes molecules at the level of functional building blocks (modular components) rather than atoms, creating a bilingual language model understanding both functional descriptions and molecular blocks.
contribution: mCLM with 3B parameters significantly improves chemical functions critical for drug development and synthetic accessibility compared to 7 other leading generative AI methods including GPT-5.

problem: Vision foundation models are typically static feature extractors, placing task adaptation burden entirely on downstream models.
approach: Language-Instructed Vision Embeddings (LIVE) uses language as high-level guidance to dynamically guide the vision encoder at inference time to produce task-centric embeddings without task-specific retraining.
contribution: LIVE reduces visual hallucinations by 34 points on MMVP, outperforms larger vision-language models on visual QA, and generalizes to unseen instructions and tasks.

problem: Existing VLM-based autonomous driving methods rely on passive perception and text-based reasoning, lacking the ability to actively seek visual evidence when uncertain.
approach: DriveAgent-R1 enables active perception for planning by proactively invoking tools for visual reasoning, combined with a hybrid thinking framework that adaptively switches between text-only and tool-augmented reasoning based on scene complexity.
contribution: With only 3B parameters, DriveAgent-R1 achieves competitive performance on Drive-Internal and nuScenes comparable to GPT-5 and human driving proficiency through Cascaded RL training.

problem: Existing segmentation models struggle to handle diverse concept prompts combining multiple modalities and to track objects across video frames.
approach: SAM 3 introduces Promptable Concept Segmentation that accepts short noun phrases, image exemplars, or combinations as prompts, using a data engine producing 4M unique concept labels and decoupling recognition from localization.
contribution: SAM 3 delivers a 2x gain over existing systems in both image and video concept segmentation while improving interactive visual segmentation capabilities.

problem: Traditional oversmoothing metrics based on feature similarity fail to reliably capture performance degradation in deep graph neural networks.
approach: The paper proposes measuring oversmoothing via numerical or effective rank of feature representations, showing rank-based metrics capture performance drops aligned with degradation where energy-based metrics fail.
contribution: Rank-based metrics consistently capture oversmoothing across diverse graph architectures and datasets, with theoretical support clarifying why Dirichlet-like measures may fail.

problem: Joint-embedding self-supervised learning struggles to flexibly capture uncertainty when each datum maps to multiple valid targets in one-to-many conditional distributions.
approach: AdaSSL introduces a variational distribution modeling conditional uncertainty in latent space with a lower bound on pairwise mutual information, also proposing a simpler sparsity-regularized variant.
contribution: AdaSSL applies to both contrastive and predictive SSL methods, improving identifiability, generalization, fine-grained image understanding, and world modeling on videos.

problem: Real-world multivariate time series forecasting must simultaneously address complex inter-channel dependencies, sampling asynchrony, and missing values, which existing architectures handle only in isolation.
approach: ChannelTokenFormer is a Transformer-based framework with flexible architecture explicitly capturing cross-channel interactions, accommodating asynchronous sampling, and effectively handling missing values.
contribution: ChannelTokenFormer demonstrates superior robustness and accuracy on public benchmarks and a private industrial dataset under challenging real-world conditions.
